title: Pickfall – a mining incremental game: swing your pickaxe, launch more, and dig down to find what's at the bottom. Free demo out on Steam
author: SparePotato147
selftext:
Hi everyone! We're OverCapacity Studios, a team of 3 people from Palestine, and Pickfall is our first game. Its free demo is out now on Steam.
    
    
    We wanted to make a mining incremental with a new twist: instead of mining just to upgrade, there is an end goal down below.
    
    
    How it plays: you swing your own pickaxe, breaking rocks launches new pickaxes that bounce around with real physics and they break the rocks on their own. Every round starts from the surface, you spend what you dug up on unlocks and upgrades, and you go deeper the next round.
    
    
    The shaft has an end. What's waiting at the bottom? You'll have to dig down and see.
    
    
    The demo is the first map with special pickaxes and blocks, around 2 hours, with more maps, upgrades and mechanics to come in the full game. It's in 24 languages.
    
    
    Play the demo and tell us what you think, good or bad. Don't hold back: give us your harshest feedback. We can take it, it will help us make the game better. And if you like it and you want to support us, a wishlist will helpus more than you'd think.
    
    
    Free demo on Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/5510260/Pickfall/
    Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9cuwyQNSWME
    
    
    AI disclosure:
    Code Art and text was generated by AI, reviewed and edited by us.
    Translation to 24 languages was done by AI
    no AI sounds, we used CC0 sources
    
    we used Claude as the main AI model for development and GPT for asset generation and doing initial reviews all through claude, godot-ai as the engine MCP and a bunch of skills some are from github repos and some made by us.
    
    since this is our first game and we where still learning we went through a lot of changes and mistakes, at first we worked in the project as if we are making any other website or app till we realised that making games is way different, so it took us hundreds of sessions and trying different workflows till we reached this state of the game.
    
    and the most annoying step was balancing, claude always tried to overcomplicat the process and it took me about a week of work, playtesting and tweaking, i would love to hear your stories on how you handled balancing an incremental game using AI, maybe it will help us in any future project.
